podcast.body: Credited as the first modern music video, "Bohemian Rhapsody" broke new ground by being shot on videotape rather than film, and it was a conceptual piece, not just a band performance. Freddie Mercury was inspired by Queen's second album cover for its visual concept. The video was created as a workaround for British Musicians Union rules prohibiting lip-syncing on TV, which made a faithful live performance of the complex song impossible. Shot in just three hours, it cost approximately $3,500 ($21,000 today) and was instrumental in turning Queen into global superstars. "It means Bohemian Rhapsody is credited as being the first modern music video."

podcast.body: Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody," originally released in 1975, became the most streamed rock song of the 21st century, having been accessed close to two billion times by the end of the 2010s. Its resurgence was partially attributed to the Queen biopic, but its massive streaming numbers highlight the enduring power of classic rock. "The most streamed rock song of the 21st century is Queen's Bohemian Rhapsody, which was released in 1975. By the end of the 2010s, it had been accessed close to two billion times."

podcast.body: The Trews used to cover Queen's iconic song "Bohemian Rhapsody" in their early cover band days, where it "always brought the house down." During their tour with Robert Plant, a fan dared them to play a "punky version" of it, which led to a standing ovation but also to Robert Plant's strong disapproval. "I heard you guys used to cover Bohemian Rhapsody in your like cover band days and it always brought the house down."

podcast.body: The reissued single of "Bohemian Rhapsody" in 1991 was the last genuine rock song to achieve the UK Christmas singles chart number one spot for nearly two decades. Following this, the position was predominantly taken by TV talent show winners or novelty tracks until Rage Against the Machine's "Killing in the Name" broke the streak in 2009. "There hadn't been a genuine rock song to finish at number one since the reissue of Queen's Bohemian Rhapsody in 1991."
